## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

# Sort in_review items in the Herdr selection list (WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

The `In Review` section of the Herdr selection list is ordered only by priority today, so producers and agents must scan the entire review queue to find actionable items; the desired behaviour is a deterministic sub-sort within the `In Review` group that surfaces the most urgent items first, using audit and flag state: `needsProducerReview=true` → fresh failed audit → stale failed audit → no audit → stale passed audit → remaining fresh passed audits.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing the queue** — scan the `In Review` section to decide what to review/close next.
  - *Story:* As a producer, I want failed audits (fresh first, then stale) at the top of `In Review` so the most problematic items are not buried behind un-audited or passed items.
- **Agents/dispatcher selecting review work** — pick the most urgent in_review item to act on.
  - *Story:* As an agent browsing the Herdr list, I want `needsProducerReview` items first, then failed audits, so producer-blocked work is surfaced first and the dispatcher consumes the correct head.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-Review bucket order (6 buckets):** Within the single last-positioned `In Review` group (`stage=in_review` items after regrouping), items are rendered in exactly this producer-confirmed bucket order: (1) `needsProducerReview=true` (any audit state), (2) fresh `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)==true`), (3) stale `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh==false` and `auditedAt` present), (4) no audit (`auditResult==null` or `auditedAt==null`), (5) stale `auditResult=true` (`readyToClose=true` with `isAuditFresh==false`), (6) remaining fresh `auditResult=true`. Within each bucket, items are sorted by priority `high → medium → low`, then by `id` as a deterministic tie-break.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mirrored ordering (Herdr + CLI + list):** The same bucket order applies in all `In Review` renderings: the Herdr regrouped worklist (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems`), `wl next --groups` (`src/commands/grouping.ts`), and `wl list` stage-filtered In Review queries (`wl list --stage in_review` via `src/commands/list.ts` / shared list ordering). Any view that renders the `In Review` section uses the identical bucket predicate.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cross-group regression:** Non-`in_review` groups (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`) keep their existing group order and within-group sort (`in_progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining`, then priority). Exactly one `In Review` section still renders, positioned last, with no duplicate headings.
- [ ] **AC4 — Freshness uses `isAuditFresh`:** `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, 60 s buffer) is the sole freshness predicate; flag-only flips of `needsProducerReview` do not make an audit stale (per WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R), and `auditedAt == updatedAt` atomics keep an immediately-audited item fresh. Stale buckets require `auditedAt` present; absence is the "no audit" bucket, not stale.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests & docs:** Unit tests cover every bucket (fresh-failed, stale-failed, no audit, stale-passed, fresh-passed, plus `needsProducerReview` precedence) with priority and `id` tie-break within a bucket, plus regroup/list integration tests that the merged Herdr list, `wl next`, and `wl list --stage in_review` all honour the bucket order; grouping comments/README note the 6-bucket order and reference this work item.
- [ ] **AC6 — Duplicate coverage:** `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` requirements are fully subsumed by this item's ACs; close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate of this item.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new ordering, including `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, and list/next command tests.

> Standard criteria also apply:
> - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
> - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep bucket logic pure and dependency-free inside the sort path (same duplication rationale as `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Herdr has zero npm deps; a mirrored implementation is required in `src/commands/grouping.ts`/`list.ts`/`next.ts` so Herdr and CLI render identically).
- Reuse `isAuditFresh` from `@worklog/shared/icons` — do not re-implement freshness.
- Do not change how `In Review` membership is decided (still `stage=in_review` regardless of `status`/`priority`); this item only reorders inside the group.

## Existing state

- Herdr `In Review` today holds all `stage=in_review` items (critical-excluded) as a single group rendered last, sorted by `compareGroupableItems` (stage tie → priority → `id`); no audit/flag bucketing.
- `WorkItem` carries `needsProducerReview?: boolean`, `auditResult?: boolean|null`, `auditedAt?: string|null`, `updatedAt?: string`; `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/helpers.ts`/`grouping.ts`) populates them and `isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) defines staleness (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`).
- `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement group order `Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review`; `selectWorkItems`/`fetchNextItems` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) compose the final displayed list preserved by regrouping.
- `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` ("Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status", `open`, `medium`, `sortIndex 7300`) described a compatible but incomplete bucket phrasing (`needsProducerReview → missing audit → stale → passed`) that omitted the fresh/stale-failed distinction; per producer confirmation it is a duplicate of this item and should be closed.
- `wl list --stage in_review` today returns `isAuditFresh`-agnostic order; `wl next --groups` groups `In Review` but does not bucket-sort it.
- Related past fixes: `WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW` (duplicate In Review sections + group order), `WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW` (in_review stage filter), `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` (atomic `auditedAt=updatedAt`).

## Desired change

- Extend the `In Review` rendering order so that after the canonical group assignment, items inside group `In Review` are stable-sorted by the 6-bucket order `(needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed)` with secondary `priority` + `id` ordering. Apply it in: (a) the Herdr regroup path (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems` / new `compareInReviewItems` helper used for the In Review slice), (b) the CLI grouping path (`src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` grouping emission), and (c) the CLI list path (`src/commands/list.ts` or the shared list sort) so `wl list --stage in_review` renders the same order. Keep the overall contracts (no filtering, deterministic ordering, mandatory items preserved) and ensure Herdr and CLI agree.
- Close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate once coverage is verified.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `regroupWorkItems` extension + new `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` helper for the 6-bucket order; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — bucket-order tests for all 6 buckets, priority/`id` tie-break, plus regroup integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — mirrored `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for CLI grouping so `wl next --groups` matches Herdr.
- `src/commands/list.ts` (+ shared list-sort helper if used) — apply same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` (and any filtered list rendering In Review).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — ensure grouped `In Review` emission honours the bucket order.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — mirrored CLI bucket-order tests.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt behaviour).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem` (reference; field availability).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — extend if In Review rendering order is asserted there.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and grouping code comments — document the 6-bucket In Review order.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV** — "Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status" (`open`, `medium`) — duplicate intent confirmed by producer; to be closed as `duplicate` of this item (this brief subsumes its requirements; its `needsProducerReview → missing → stale → passed` phrasing is a shorthand for the full 6-bucket order defined here).
- **WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW** — "Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order)" (`completed`, `medium`) — established the single last-positioned `In Review` section and Critical/Group N file-path grouping preserved here.
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** — "Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items because stage-filtered fetch restricts to status=open" (`completed`, `high`) — established that `in_review` items carry `completed`/`in-progress` status and must be fetched specially.
- **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 / WL-0MTHRW3770014H51** — atomic `saveAuditResult: updatedAt=auditedAt` and `isAuditFresh` 60 s window; governs the fresh vs stale distinction used by buckets 2/3/5/6.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** — "Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head" (`in-progress`, `critical`) — dispatcher that will consume the newly-ordered head; consuming the sorted In Review order is the downstream value.
- **WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z** — narrow-pane header truncation (`in_review`, `high`, `needsProducerReview:true`) — unrelated rendering concern, noted only to avoid chrome-budget interaction.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale vs fresh failed precedence:** Producer confirmed that fresh failed (`readyToClose=false` + fresh) outranks stale failed, and stale failed outranks `no audit`; stale passed outranks only the fresh-passed rest. Assumption: within each bucket, priority `high→medium→low` then `id` is the tie-break (from WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV's "within each group sort by priority").
- **Scope-creep risk:** Stage/priority changes inside `In Review`, new `In Review` splitting across multiple headings, or changing membership (e.g. filtering by `needsProducerReview`) are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups, not in-scope.
- **Duplication maintenance:** CLI grouping and Herdr grouping must mirror the same bucket helper to avoid divergence (same rationale as Q2c duplication); keep the logic pure and tested in both places.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is the exact bucket order inside `In Review`? The description lists needsProducerReview=true first, then audit with readyToClose=false, then no audit, then stale audit, then the rest — but related WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV phrases it as needsProducerReview=true, followed by audit missing, followed by audit stale then audit passed (no mention of the readyToClose=false bucket). Please confirm the canonical 5-bucket order and whether stale-failed and stale-passed both belong in the stale bucket or if failed audits should always outrank stale audits." — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "needsProducerReview=true → audit readyToClose=false → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → rest". Interpretation applied: 6 buckets = `needsProducerReview` → fresh `readyToClose=false` → stale `readyToClose=false` → no audit → stale `readyToClose=true` → fresh `readyToClose=true` (within each bucket: high→medium→low→id). The first `readyToClose=false` bucket is fresh-failed; the explicit `stale-failed` bucket is stale-failed; stale-passed is stale-passed. Source: interactive reply. Research: inspected `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:279` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (In Review single-last group), `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (WorkItem fields), `src/commands/grouping.ts` (CLI grouping).
- Q: "Should `needsProducerReview` be a bucket for the whole In Review group or a flag that just bubbles flagged items to the very front regardless of audit status?" — Answer (producer, implied by bucket list): it is the topmost bucket covering the whole group — any `needsProducerReview=true` item precedes every non-flagged In Review item regardless of audit state.
- Q: "Does the bucket order apply only to the Herdr plugin or also to `wl next --groups` / CLI In Review rendering?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl next mirrors" — CLI grouping mirrors the Herdr bucket order so both render identically.
- Q: "Should `wl list --stage in_review` and the `--priority`/`--status` filtered lists also apply the same In Review bucket order, or only the default/browse worklist?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl list shows same ordering" — the same 6-bucket order applies to `wl list` In Review renderings.
- Q: "WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV describes a near-duplicate sort for in_review items. Should it be closed as a duplicate of this item after intake, or kept as a separate follow-up?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "close as duplicate (check this item covers all requirements)" — WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV closes as duplicate of this item; this brief explicitly subsumes its requirements (see AC6 and Related work).
- Additional related docs inspected: `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/list.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `wl show WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV --json`.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Extend `regroupWorkItems` with `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for the 6-bucket Herdr In Review order (`needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed`, priority/`id` tie-break).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Add 6-bucket and priority tie-break tests + merged-list In Review bucket integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` — Mirror the same bucket helper for `wl next --groups` CLI In Review grouping.
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Apply the same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` filtered In Review rendering.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem`.

Mechanism under investigation: wl update --needs-producer-review bumps updatedAt (packages/shared/src/database.ts update()); herdr's isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts) then reports stale, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon and (b) re-selects the item for audit-tier dispatch (selectAuditCandidate, packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts).

data.description: Sometimes work items get left stuck in in_progress. Every 30 seconds the herdr plugin should retrieve all in_progress work items and attempt to match an active pane to the work item. If none is found then set to either completed, blocked or open. This work item should be blocked on the one to add work item id to pane titles, which can then be used to match panes. All tabs in the current workspace should be searched.
data.title: Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
